{{nihongo|'''Hinamajihimemikoto Shrine'''|比奈麻治比売命神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Nishinoshima, Shimane|Q543193|qid=Q543193}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|Q735735|qid=Q735735}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} (minor shrine), and its former shrine rank was village shrine. It is commonly known as '''Sumi (Sun) Daimyōjin'''. {{nihongo|'''Hinamajihimemikoto Shrine'''|比奈麻治比売命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Oki Province]].

== Overview ==
Originally, Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto Shrine was located on a mountain above “Sumi-no-ura,” at the northeastern tip of {{ill|Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Q5004035|qid=Q5004035}}{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=67}}. It is an ancient shrine whose name appears in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}} from as early as the 8th century, and the divine power of its enshrined deity, '''Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto''', is thought to be related to {{ill|Fire|Q3196|qid=Q3196}}{{sfn|Rika-no-Ya|1987|pp=232–233}}. It is also listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}', but after the medieval period it ceased to appear in historical records{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=944}}. In the early modern period, it reappears in documents under names such as “Sumi Daimyōjin” as the {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}} of the Uga area. Because its location was inconvenient for worship as an ubusuna shrine, it was ultimately relocated in Shōwa 3 (1928) to its present site closer to the settlement{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=67}}.

== Enshrined deity ==
{{see also|#Legends}}
; Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto
From the miraculous accounts described below, the deity’s divine power is thought to be connected with fire, and the name “Hinamachi” is interpreted as “true spirit of fire”{{sfn|Rika-no-Ya|1987|pp=232–233}}{{sfn|Matsuura|1987|p=37}}. From the medieval period onward, tales of the sacred fire came to be confused with episodes of {{ill|Takuhi Shrine|Q11567668|qid=Q11567668}}{{sfn|Rika-no-Ya|1987|p=233}}. She is sometimes regarded as another name for {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iku-tamayori-hime}}, but this is thought to reflect the intentions of the shrine family{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=944}}. Concerning the sacred object, a shrine inspection diary from Meiji 2 records “the sacred body is a wooden statue,” while an old survey ledger states “a black stone (omitted)… might this truly be the sacred body”{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=69}}.

Within Shimane Prefecture, she is enshrined only at Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto Shrine{{sfn|Rika-no-Ya|1987|p=233}}, but within the grounds of Kashima Shrine in {{ill|Izumo, Shimane|Q825166|qid=Q825166}}, the subsidiary Himori Shrine enshrines “Hinamochi-hime-no-Mikoto”{{sfn|Ōgi-no-Ya|1987|p=228}}. Formerly, at {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himine Shrine}} in {{ill|Kitakyushu|Q188806|qid=Q188806}}, Fukuoka Prefecture, a tradition stated: “The deity Hinamachihime of Oki Province manifested on this mountain; therefore a shrine was established and worshiped,” and she was enshrined as the principal deity{{sfn|Onga District Board of Education, ed.|1986|pp=1145–1147}}.

== Facilities ==
== Present site ==
[[File:Hinamadihime honden.jpg|thumb|300px|Main hall of Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto Shrine]]
; Shrine buildings
* Main hall – A modified {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}} style with a frontage of 1.5 ken and a depth of 1.5 ken{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=945}} (Kasuga-zukuri with corner rafters{{sfn|Makabe & Kuroda|2016|p=544}}).
* Worship hall – Frontage 4 ken, depth 4 ken{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=945}}.
; Subsidiary shrines
Misaki Shrine, Tenman Shrine, and Hachidai Ryūō Shrine were merged into this shrine in Meiji 40 (1907){{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=312}}{{efn|There are also accounts stating that Tenman Shrine was merged in Meiji 13 (1880) or at the end of the Taishō period, and Misaki Shrine at the end of the Taishō period{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=68}}{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=314}}.}}. At the time of the relocation in Shōwa 3 (1928), they were left at the former site, but in Shōwa 45 (1970) they were moved to the precincts of the present site{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=312}}.
* Misaki Shrine – A wooden shrine dedicated to a water deity{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}. Formerly located near the residence of the Yokoya (priest, the Uno family){{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=314}}.
* Tenman Shrine – A wooden shrine dedicated to Tenjin{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}. Formerly located in a place called “Tenjin Yashiki”{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=314}}. A {{ill|Nobori|Q1068772|qid=Q1068772}} bearing the ink inscription “Namu Myōhō Renge Kyō” is offered{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}.
* Hachidai Ryūō Shrine – A stone monument inscribed “White Dragon King Deity”{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=312}}. The former site is unknown{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=314}}.
; Shrine office
Uses a remodeled lodging hut{{efn|After praying to the ubusuna shrine for recovery from illness, safe childbirth, abundant catches, school admission, etc., there was a custom called “okomori,” in which one would spend the night in a hut within the shrine precincts called a “komosha” or “komoriya” as thanks for the fulfillment of the prayer{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=310}}.}}{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}.

== Former site ==
Located on a mountain above “Sumi-no-ura”{{efn|Also written “Sun”{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=943}}.}} at the northeastern tip of Nishinoshima{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=943}}. A stone monument marking the former site was erected in Shōwa 45 (1970){{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}.
* Main hall – A modified Kasuga-zukuri with a frontage of 1 ken and a depth of 1.5 ken{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=945}}. Beneath the main hall, a stone is buried, with its upper part exposed above ground{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}.

== History ==
According to an entry from Enryaku 18 (799) in the '{{ill|Nihon Kōki|Q1077029|qid=Q1077029}}', {{ill|Kura no Sukune Kamo-maro|ja|内蔵賀茂麻呂|qid=Q45828962|lt=Kura no Sukune Kamo-maro}}, a member of a {{ill|Japanese missions to Balhae|ja|遣渤海使|ko|견발해사|zh|遣渤海使|qid=Q11642473}} who had drifted at sea, relied on a firelight miracle granted by Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto to return safely, leading to the shrine being elevated to an officially supported shrine{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=69}}. The place where Kura no Sukune is said to have landed is called “Kuranotani”{{efn|There is also a tradition identifying a place called “Kurashiki” as where he landed and rested{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=69}}.}}, and this area falls within the parish of Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto Shrine{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}.

In Shōwa 5 (838), the shrine’s deity was promoted from no rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|cs|Šoku Nihonkóki|de|Shoku Nihon Kōki|es|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ff|Shoku Nihon Kōki|fr|Shoku nihon kōki|ja|続日本後紀|ko|속일본후기|pt|Shoku Nihon Kōki|zh|續日本後紀|qid=Q1041301}}); in Jōgan 13 (871), from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}); and in Gangyō 2 (878), from Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade (Sandai Jitsuroku), reflecting successive promotions in {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=944}}. It is also listed as a minor Shikinaisha in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}'{{sfn|Takahashi et al., eds.|1996|p=477}}.

For some time thereafter, the shrine did not appear in historical records, but perhaps because it was located in an isolated area away from settlements, its rites continued quietly without being supplanted by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kanjō}} deities{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=944}}.

In the early modern period, references appear again: as “Sun Daimyōjin” in the 'Zōshin Inshūki' of Jōkyō 5 (1688), as “Sumi Daimyōjin” in the 'Ryōtō Jinja Shoaget-chō' of Hōreki 7 (1757), and as “Sun Shrine” in the late Edo-period 'Oki Kokiki-shū'{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=944}}.

Originally, the shrine was enshrined near the coast at Sumi-no-ura due to its miraculous power, but as it came to be venerated as an {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}}, the site proved inconvenient for worship. Thus, in Ansei 2 (1855), it was relocated once to a place called Makome{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=67}}{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=945}}. In Meiji 13 (1880), it was returned to the former site following a divine oracle, but again found inconvenient, leading to another relocation closer to the settlement{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=68}}{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}{{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=943}}. At the initially proposed site of Tsukatani, a fatal accident occurred during construction for the relocation, so in Shōwa 3 (1928) the shrine was moved to a place called “Biya,” where it remains today{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}. Because this relocation was approved under the pretext of establishing a village shrine, the former site could not be completely abolished{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=68}}, and the subsidiary shrines remained there until they were moved to “Biya” in Shōwa 45 (1970){{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=312}}.

== Legends ==
* It is said that the enshrined deity, Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto, drifted ashore and landed at a place called “Kantsuki (divine landing),” slightly south of the inlet of Sumi{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=69}}.
* Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto is said to be married to '''Uwaga-no-Mikoto''', the enshrined deity of {{ill|Ujika Shrine|ja|宇受賀命神社|qid=Q11449116}} in {{ill|Ama, Shimane|ar|أما|arz|اما|be|Ама (Сіманэ)|ceb|Ama Chō|es|Ama (Shimane)|fa|اما، شیمان|fr|Ama (Shimane)|hu|Ama|id|Ama, Shimane|it|Ama (Shimane)|ja|海士町|ko|아마정|ms|Ama, Shimane|my|အမမြို့၊ ရှိမနဲ|pl|Ama (Shimane)|ro|Ama, Shimane|ru|Ама (посёлок)|sv|Ama, Shimane|tl|Ama, Shimane|tr|Ama, Shimane|ur|اما، شیمانے|zh|海士町|qid=Q685865}}{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=73}}. Furthermore, their child is said to be '''Nakirahime-no-Mikoto''', the enshrined deity of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakirahime Shrine}} in Ama Town{{sfn|Kamada|1960|p=73}}. Uwaga-no-Mikoto is said to have competed with the {{ill|Ooyama Shrine|ja|大山神社 (西ノ島町)|qid=Q11434677|lt=deity of Mount Ōyama}} over Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto. When she declared she would marry whoever won a contest of strength, they competed by throwing {{ill|Pebble|an|Ruello (glera)|ar|حصى الشواطئ|az|Çınqıl|bat_smg|Žvirzdos|be|Галька|be_x_old|Галька|bew|Kolar|br|Bili|ca|Còdol|cdo|Siŏh-tàu-lâung|ce|Сицкъар|cs|Kačírek|cv|Шакă|da|Ral (geologi)|el|Βότσαλο|eo|Ŝtoneto|es|Canto rodado|et|Veeris|eu|Errekarri|fa|ریگ|fj|Vatu lailai|fr|Galet|ga|Cloch dhuirlinge|gan|磨硌牯子|gl|Canto rolado|he|חלוק נחל|hu|Kavics|id|Kerakal|io|Stono|it|Ciottolo|ja|礫|ka|კენჭი|kk|Малталар|ko|조약돌|ky|Галька|lfn|Calculo (jeolojia)|li|Kezelstein|lt|Žvirgždas|mg|Vatokilonjy|nap|Vreccia|nl|Kiezelsteen|nn|Rullestein|no|Rullestein|oc|Arrebòt|om|Cancullee|pl|Otoczak (geologia)|pnb|کنکر|pt|Seixo|ro|Balast (material de construcție)|ru|Галька|sah|Чай|simple|Pebble|sk|Obliak|sn|Hurungudo|sv|Klapperstenar|ta|கூழாங்கல்|th|กรวดกลาง|to|Foʻi maka|tr|Çakıl taşı|tt|Чагырташ|uk|Галька|ur|کنکر|vi|Cuội (đá)|wa|Bidinne|wuu|卵石|zh|卵石|zh_min_nan|Chio̍h-nn̄g|zh_yue|石春|qid=Q14673}} at each other from their respective islands{{sfn|Nagami|1968|p=628}}. At that time, a {{ill|Amanojaku|ca|Ama-no-jaku|es|Ama-no-jaku|fa|آمانوجاکو|fr|Amanojaku|id|Amanojaku|it|Amanojaku|ja|天邪鬼|ko|아마노자쿠|pl|Amanjaku|pt|Amanojaku|ru|Аманодзяку|uk|Аманоджяку|vi|Amanojaku|zh|天邪鬼|zh_yue|天邪鬼|qid=Q2417460}} pulled at the sleeve of the Ōyama deity to interfere, resulting in Uwaga-no-Mikoto’s victory and Hinamadihime-no-Mikoto marrying him{{sfn|Nagami|1968|p=628}}.
* A small golden snake that emerged from the white waves and came ashore at a place called “Mejika” is regarded as the shrine’s {{ill|Shinshi|fr|Shinshi|ja|神使|simple|Shinshi|zh|神使|qid=Q10444973}}. It is said that this snake prevents impure persons from approaching the shrine{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}.

== Festivals ==
The festival is held on July 28{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}{{efn|Before the adoption of the Gregorian calendar following the relocation in Shōwa 3 (1928), it was held on June 28 of the lunar calendar{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}.}}. When the shrine was located at Sumi-no-ura, only the Yokoya (priest) and parish representatives participated; in calm seas they traveled by boat, and in rough weather they used mountain paths to visit the shrine{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=311}}. After the relocation to Biya, {{ill|Kagura|ar|كاغورا|ca|Kagura|cs|Kagura|de|Kagura|es|Kagura (danza)|fa|کاگورا|fi|Kagura|fr|Kagura|id|Kagura|it|Kagura (danza)|ja|神楽|ko|가구라|lt|Kagura|ms|Kagura|or|କାଗୁରା|pl|Kagura|pt|Kagura|ru|Кагура|sq|Kagura|te|కగుర (నృత్య రీతి)|tr|Kagura|uk|Каґура|vi|Kagura|zh|神樂|qid=Q1348260}} performances came to be offered, and upon completion of the festival the parish representatives, district head, and priest held a naorai (ritual feast){{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|pp=311–312}}. General worshippers receive {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sacred sake}} at the shrine{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=312}}.

The ujigami-kō (parish association ritual) is held on January 28{{sfn|Ōtsu|1973|p=322}}.
